subject: Q4 GPU reservation decision: balancing two enterprise commitments
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity arbitration request — two consecutive Q4 commitments

Team,

Putting this thread together because we have two enterprise deals that both require dedicated capacity in a tight Q4 window and procurement deadlines are imminent. High-level: 

- NimbusHealth (Tom Ridley) — needs committed 40 A100-equivalent GPUs for inference/rescoring & model variants, preferred start: 2026-11-15; contract close expected within 48–72h if capacity is reserved.
- Aster Analytics (Sofia Morales) — needs 30 GPUs, start target: 2026-12-01, compliance window mandates capacity by Dec 1.

I've attached Q4_demand_forecast.xlsx with estimates (sheet: per-deal sizing). Both deals are high ARR but Nimbus is a strategic health partner (long-term roadmap alignment). We currently have limited free Dedicated pool for the US region in November — Karthik, can you confirm raw availability and mitigation levers? Lauren, can we surface contractual levers (start date flexibility, staggered ramp, premium for guaranteed reservation)?

Goal: quick internal decision on allocation policy (reserve full for first signed; split; premium-backed reservation; or push Aster to burst-only until Jan). I propose a 1-hour alignment call today if possible.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: Q4_demand_forecast.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity arbitration request — two consecutive Q4 commitments

Marcus — thanks for the summary. Important context from GTM: Nimbus is high strategic priority (partner program, potential co-sell), and their legal/infosec timeline is tight once we commit. Aster is high-value and fast-growing, but we may have more contract flexibility there.

Ask: Karthik, provide a worst-case and best-case footprint for November–January (steady state + peak) and list operational risks if we try to squeeze both in. Lauren, once Karthik posts his numbers, propose two commercial options we can offer: 1) premium reservation for Nimbus to guarantee start date; 2) staggered start for Aster with guaranteed minimum reservation + burst allowance.

I want a recommendation within 24 hours so we can respond to Nimbus’ urgency.

-Neha
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity arbitration request — two consecutive Q4 commitments (capacity analysis)

Folks,

I ran the pool-level simulation for US Dedicated clusters and attached the per-deal tab in Q4_demand_forecast.xlsx. Short summary:

- Current committed Dedicated capacity (US): 480 A100-equivalent GPUs.
- Scheduled reserves (existing deals + known renewals) through Nov: 430 GPUs.
- Free/nominal available pool for new reservations in mid-Nov: ~50 GPUs.

Options to fit both deals:
1) Reserve Nimbus full (40 GPUs) for 11/15 start, and offer Aster a staggered reservation: 20 GPUs guaranteed on 12/01 and access to a 20-GPU burst bucket (best-effort) for peaks. Risk: Aster will see throughput variability under peak; potential latency regressions for their strict SLOs.
2) Compress Aster with quantized model profiles (8-bit) and batching optimizations to reduce equivalent footprint to ~18–22 GPUs. This will need engineering validation and could delay Aster’s go-live by ~2 weeks.
3) Short-term overcommit with strict preemption rules: allow Aster to consume capacity but preempt down to 10 GPUs when Nimbus is in heavy production. High operational complexity and possible churn.

My recommendation: go with option (1) unless Aster’s contract cannot accept burst / variability. We can also offer Aster a discounted premium to secure more guaranteed units.

Attachments included: Q4_demand_forecast.xlsx (per-deal simulation).

-Karthik
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Ridley <tom.ridley@nimbushealth.io>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: ellie.park@procure-helix.com
Date: 2026-10-05T16:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: (External) Capacity arbitration request — NimbusHealth commitment

Marcus — thanks for the heads up. Quick note from our side: Nimbus will move to sign if we receive a firm written commitment that 40 A100-equivalent GPUs are reserved and available for production by 2026-11-15. Health compliance timelines and partner integrations are already scheduled around that date — we cannot shift. If Redwood can provide a reservation letter or redlined statement in the MSA addendum, we'll countersign today.

Tom Ridley
Head of ML Products, NimbusHealth
tridley@nimbushealth.io
From: Sofia Morales <sofia@asteranalytics.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: Ellie Park <ellie.park@procure-helix.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: (External) Capacity arbitration request — Aster Analytics timeline

Marcus, 

Appreciate the transparency. Aster’s compliance window starts Dec 1 and we need 30 GPUs by then. We can be flexible on how the capacity is delivered (staged ramp OK) but cannot accept a slip past Dec 10. Our procurement team (Ellie cc’d) is ready to execute once you confirm guaranteed minimums. If there is a premium for guaranteed units, please outline it.

Sofia Morales
VP, Infrastructure & ML, Aster Analytics
sofia@asteranalytics.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Ridley <tom.ridley@nimbushealth.io>, Sofia Morales <sofia@asteranalytics.com>, Ellie Park <ellie.park@procure-helix.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Decision & next steps — temporary allocation plan (internal + customer note)

Following the analysis and customer priorities, here's the allocation path I propose for immediate commercial follow-up: 

1) NimbusHealth — commit: reserve 40 GPUs starting 2026-11-15 through 2027-01-15 as a paid reserved block. Sales ops to produce a reservation addendum and a signed reservation letter to Nimbus on receipt of a counter-signed PO. (Lauren: please draft with legal; include a premium reservation fee and SLA guarantees.)

2) Aster Analytics — offer: guaranteed 20 GPUs from 2026-12-01 and access to a 20-GPU burst pool (best-effort) up to Dec 31. We will include a carve-out in the SOW that guarantees no reduction below 20 GPUs and documents burst best-effort behavior; offer an optional premium to increase guaranteed units. (Neha: confirm pricing flexibility.)

3) Engineering mitigations: Karthik will work with runtime to validate a quantized deployment profile for Aster to reduce steady-state footprint; try to reclaim additional capacity by end of December.

4) Contingency: If Nimbus fails to sign within 72 hours, revert and re-evaluate allocations — we will keep both customers informed.

Marcus (for transparency, I’ll forward a version of this to both customers as the commercial proposal).

Next steps assigned: Lauren (reservation addendum), Neha (pricing for Aster burst/premium), Karthik (engineering runbook for quantization + monitoring to detect SLO regressions).

Thanks — Marcus
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: NimbusHealth_deal_summary.pdf; AsterAnalytics_statement_of_work.docx
